correctness.rationale: The Boolean rim update is OR with a one-hub and AND with a zero-hub. For every even n>=12, a contiguous initial run of length n/2-4 grows by two for four updates and shrinks by two for four, with hub sequence 11110000 enforced by strict minority decisions and the two half-rim ties. Endpoint locations return exactly, while the four-step hub differs. For odd n the one dissenter is a pure anti-threshold vertex on a loopless graph, so Haslegrave–Cannings (arXiv:1606.05496v1, Theorem 10) excludes period eight. Complete independent exhaustive code evaluates all 2^(n+1) states for the four even n<12 and n=12; both implementations return zero at n<12 and 288 at n=12. The 36 temporal orbits follow by division by eight. Tests at greater n supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies an exact parity and size threshold for a dynamical period excluded by the classical pure anti-threshold theorem on loopless graphs. It proves infinitely many explicit primitive-eight waves with a natural one-dissenter voting rule, and exactly determines the first admissible state population. The tie-retention mechanism and endpoint-wave construction are structural rather than a routine generic period-existence observation.
